title: Deep Hierarchical Semantic Segmentation (HSSN)
mechanism: Pixel-wise multi-label classification over a class tree, with a tree-min loss that keeps child scores at or below their parent, plus hierarchy-based embedding margins.
adaptation: A 2-level tree: cell area -> feature lines (gridline, busbar, ribbon, splice), defects (crack, inactive, material, corrosion), and the rest. Add parent sigmoid channels with tree-min consistency and keep softmax leaves. Aimed at splice (never predicted) and gridline (recall 0.33).
min_experiment: Arm: house + parent channels + tree-min loss. Baseline: house. Metrics: gridline, splice and material IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and splice stays at 0.
evidence: R: gains on Mapillary Vistas 2.0, Cityscapes, LIP and PASCAL-Person-Part across backbones. The abstract page gives no numbers.

alt_notes.adaptation: Two-level tree: cell area -> {structural lines: gridline, busbar, ribbon, splice; defects: crack, inactive, material, corrosion}; parent sigmoid channels + tree-min, leaves stay softmax; target splice (0.000) and gridline (0.283).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house + parent channels + tree-min; baseline house; metrics gridline, splice, edge_dark IoU, mIoU_rob; kill if mIoU_rob gain < 0.01 and splice still 0.
